candidates.lead: Pat Karney, who had been receiving treatment for cancer, had sat on Manchester City Council since 1979
candidates.evidence_text: Pat Karney: Tributes to Manchester political giant - BBC News Image source, Manchester City Council Image caption, Pat Karney has died aged 78 By Marc Waddington North West Published 1 hour ago Tributes have been paid to "a giant" of Manchester's political scene on his death at the age of 78. Pat Karney had represented Harpurhey for Labour since 1979 and had been well-known as the authority's city centre spokesman. He had been suffering from cancer and had been having treatment at The Christie hospital. Manchester City Council leader Garry Bridges said he was "Manchester through and through and he never lost his determination to champion the city or his astute political judgement". Karney was born in Dublin and moved to Manchester as a boy. Proud of his Irish roots, he played a prominent role in the city's Irish Festival. He helped drive the regeneration of Manchester city centre following the 1996 IRA bombing and masterminded the first Manchester Day celebrations in 2010. A long-standing champion of gay rights, he also played a leading role in Manchester City Council's opposition to Section 28, which prohibited local authorities and state-funded schools from "promoting homosexuality". 'Great sense of fun' Bridges said: "Pat was a giant of Manchester politics and one of the city's most recognisable public figures for nearly 50 years. "He never lost his connection to where he came from. He was proud to be from Collyhurst and to represent the people of Harpurhey and Collyhurst." He said that although Karney was "deeply serious about his politics and his values", he also had "a great sense of fun" and was not afraid to use "a gimmick or two" to get his message across. "For us in the council, we knew the Pat that everyone else knew, but we also knew him as a friend, someone who was always there with sage advice. "We will miss him personally as much as we will miss him politically." Chief executive Tom Stannard said he would miss Karney's "wisdom, his generosity with time and his inimitable grasp of Manchester's history, as well as his forever optimism about its future". Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig said: "Across Manchester and across politics, many will mourn the loss of Pat Karney, a force of nature who served our city for half a century. "My thoughts are with his family, who he treasured and adored, at this difficult time. He will always be in our hearts." candidates.lead: Patsy McKie dedicated her life to bringing about change after gang violence spiralled in Manchester
candidates.evidence_text: Mural remembers anti-crime campaigner who lost son to gun crime - BBC News Image caption, Patsy McKie set up Mothers Against Violence days after her son was shot dead in 1999 By Kelly Foran and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 2 hours ago A mural has been created to honour the legacy of an anti-crime campaigner who was inspired to act after her son's death. Patsy McKie's youngest son Dorrie, 20, was shot dead in the Hulme area of Manchester in 1999. Just days later, she co-founded Mothers Against Violence (MAVUK) and dedicated the rest of her life to travelling across the world to raise awareness of her anti-crime campaign. A colourful mural has been painted at the MAVUK Hulme Centre following her death in January 2025 at the age of 77. "She was a very bright person, even through some of the most difficult periods of her life," said her son, Ian Swanston. "She wanted to bring a sense of colour to the world. "A creative artwork representing Patsy would have to be colourful, because that's definitely what she wants." Image caption, Patsy McKie began campaigning against violent crime after her son's death Dorrie has been about to start a sports and leisure course at college when he was shot dead amid spiralling gang violence in Manchester. Patsy believed deeply in the strength of community and in the possibility of healing, even during the most difficult of times. "She always said that if young people are doing something positive, they won't have time to do the things that are negative in our community," said Ian. "So she really wanted to be able to create spaces that allowed young people to excel." MAVUK was set up to support families to fight injustice, achieve their full potential and participate actively in their communities. "I think she always wanted Hulme to be a big part of her life story," said Ian. "I think she really treasured the place that she lived." Makisa Gilkes, from Jet Black Dance Academy, is just one of the people to have benefited from Patsy's work. "Born and raised in this community - and obviously in a quite deprived area - so having an area where I can develop as a person and teach other people doing dance and also to be able to do it myself and having somewhere comfortable for me to attend," she said, "it has helped us a lot". candidates.lead: Simon Richardson is accused of driving with Michael Mullins under his car while knowing he was there
candidates.evidence_text: A head teacher was dragged to his death for more than a mile trapped under the wheels of a car driven by a man who allegedly knew he was there, a jury heard Simon Richardson, 35, denies the murder of 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was struck and killed as he cycled home from work on 20 April Prosecutors claim Richardson stopped along the way, tried to dislodge the injured but still living cyclist, before driving on with Mullins remaining trapped under the wheels He also denies an alternative count of manslaughter and one of dangerous driving - relating to a police chase the following day - and is standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Philip Barnes KC, opening the case for the prosecution, told the jury that "plainly fit" Mullins was cycling from Stretford Grammar School to his home in Northwich - his usual 19-mile (30-km) commute - at 18:07 BST on Paddock Lane in Warburton, Trafford As the married father-of-two approached the junction with Dunham Road, a black Volvo XC90 drove straight through give-way signs and road markings and struck the left side of his bike

candidates.lead: Manchester City Council has made almost £3m from the "super-profits" of Man City-linked developments
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Council has made just under £3m from a deal to share in the so-called "super-profits" from developments built on its land by Manchester City's owners A deal struck in 2014 meant the council would receive payments if the profits made by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) on schemes in Ancoats and New Islington exceeded a certain level But Prof Adam Leaver, co-author of a 2022 report by the University of Sheffield into the council's relationship with ADUG, said commercial secrecy around the arrangements meant it was hard to know if the council got the best value it could The council said it expected another payment soon, and that the regeneration had been worth £1.25bn to the city In 2008, Manchester City was bought for £200m by ADUG, owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan - a senior member of the Abu Dhabi ruling family, who is a current vice president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) In the next decade, the club went on to win the first three of eight Premier League titles, and ADUG and Manchester City Council became partners in a company called Manchester Life

candidates.evidence_text: Public inquiry over Manchester synagogue attack deaths - BBC News Image source, Family handouts Image caption, Adrian Daulby, left, and Melvin Cravitz, right, were killed in the attack on the synagogue in Manchester By Daniel Wittenberg North West Published 12 October 2026 Updated 13 October 2026 A public inquiry will examine the deaths of two men killed during an attack at a synagogue in Manchester last year. Melvin Cravitz, 66, died from multiple stab wounds and fellow worshipper Adrian Daulby, 53, was killed by a bullet fired by armed police as he blocked the synagogue doors when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, tried to get in the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue on 2 October 2025. Announcing the inquiry, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said: "What happened that day must be fully understood." Syrian-born UK citizen Al-Shamie was shot dead by police while carrying out the attack. Police had already seized Al-Shamie's mobile phone containing details of his "extremist mindset", but did not analyse the contents until after he had attacked the synagogue. The attack took place on Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the year for Jews. Mahmood said: "In recent days, we marked the first anniversary of the terror attack at the Heaton Park synagogue. "On that awful day in October of last year, as our Jewish community celebrated Yom Kippur, two brave men – Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby – lost their lives, and three others were seriously injured. "What happened that day must be fully understood. "So, as requested by the coroner, I can today announce a public inquiry into the deaths of Mr Cravitz and Mr Daulby. "This will ensure that all evidence can be heard, including any sensitive national security material that could not otherwise be fully heard in the coroner's court." Image source, PA Media Image caption, Three other people were seriously injured in the 2025 attack In response to the announcement, one of the men who was seriously injured in the attack welcomed the news, calling for the public inquiry to begin "without unnecessary delay". Andrew Franks continues to recover from both the physical and psychological injuries sustained when he was stabbed in the face and neck by the attacker, after he volunteered to provide security outside the synagogue that day. In a statement issued by his lawyer, Franks described the inquiry as "essential" noting "the continuing concerns about the safety and security of Jewish communities across the United Kingdom". He said he hoped an inquiry would "provide answers for all those affected by the attack - particularly the bereaved families - whilst also ensuring that meaningful recommendations are made and acted upon. "It is vital that we do not lose momentum now that the decision to establish the inquiry has been taken. "The focus must now be on moving forward quickly, learning lessons and implementing changes that make a real difference," his lawyer added. Earlier this year a police chief said he was "deeply sorry" over missed opportunities to potentially uncover the plot to attack the synagogue. The apology came after details emerged following the jailing of Al-Shamie's friend and accomplice, Mohammad Bashir, in July. Bashir, 31, was sentenced to life imprisonment at Manchester Crown Court for planning a separate attack with Al-Shamie on the UK Defence Academy at Shrivenham. "These allegations resulted in his being arrested on the 13 February 2025 on suspicion of breaching a non-molestation order; and on the 21 September 2025 on suspicion of rape. "At the time of his committing the attack at the Heaton Park Synagogue, Al-Shamie was on police bail." 'Missed opportunity' Watson continued: "In conducting an internal review, it became apparent that GMP had seized Al-Shamie's mobile devices at the point of each arrest. "The significance of the data contents of these devices was substantial in respect of evidencing an extremist mindset. "Regrettably, I can confirm that the significance of the information stored on Al-Shamie's devices was not realised, as they had not been examined before the attack took place on the 2 October 2025. candidates.evidence_text: Our memorial garden helps us grieve - a cemetery felt too far away - BBC News Image source, Emma Moore Image caption, Emma Moore says the garden has given her family, including elder daughter Penelope, a focus following the death of baby Mabel By George Sandeman Published 14 October 2026, 01:06 BST Updated 19 minutes ago When Emma Moore's daughter Mabel died, visiting her in a cemetery felt too far away. "I don't like going to them and I feel like [visits] fizzle out," she says. "At first, you'll go regularly and then it'll start being once a year." Mabel was born prematurely at 27 weeks in April, her lungs had not fully developed and she lived for just two days. Emma keeps Mabel's ashes next to a photograph of her tiny feet but she wanted a special place to feel close to her. "So we created something in the garden... [to] always be reminded of her every day," she tells Morning Live . The stillness of green spaces "can help us connect with memories" of loved ones, says Andy Langford, clinical director at Cruse Bereavement Support. And there are ways to create a special place of calm to remember anyone you've lost - even if you don't have a garden or know much about plants. Image source, Emma Moore Image caption, Emma, with her partner Louis and daughter Penelope, says the garden reminds them of Mabel each day "I'd never done anything like this before, so I had no clue about where to start," says Emma, 35, who lives near Bolton with her partner Louis and daughter Penelope. She chose to dedicate a part of the garden with a willow tree to Mabel. "I've enjoyed doing the gardening and planting. It was nice to focus on something." Of all the flowers the family have planted in Mabel's garden, Emma's favourite are the lilies. Morning Live - Memorial Gardens Families speak about the healing power of nature and how some have created dedicated green spaces at home. Watch on iPlayer The story about memorial gardens starts at 1:02:20 White lilies are said to represent peace and are a traditional choice for acts of remembrance in the UK, says botanist James Wong of BBC Gardeners' Question Time . The flowers are low maintenance and can last for decades, he says. The colour of flowers in your garden a personal choice, adds Wong. Some may find soft pink, mauve and lilac relaxing, while others may find yellows and reds more vibrant and lift the mood. Image source, Morning Live Image caption, Emma hadn't done much gardening before but has enjoyed creating one for Mabel Wong says smell helps us connect to nature and works with the sight of beautiful flowers to create a peaceful atmosphere. Many rose varieties have a fragrance but Wong also suggests choosing plants with scented leaves for when flowers are not in bloom. "If you were to plant something like a mint, a eucalyptus or a rose geranium - they have very strongly scented leaves and they're around for a long period of time." He also suggests evergreen Italian cypresses, tall and thin plants more commonly used for commemoration in warmer climates, as they are capable of growing "perfectly well outdoors in the UK". They have a woody aroma likened to pine or juniper. Wong also says chrysanthemums - "a classic funeral flower" in East Asian cultures - will also readily grow here. They have a herbal almost medicinal fragrance. Image source, Morning Live Image caption, The family dedicated a part of their garden under a willow tree to Mabel Emma has placed a bench with a plaque featuring Mabel's name near the willow tree. She often sits on the bench in the morning with a cup of tea. "It's her little garden," says Emma. "It's a really personal space." Langford says benches are common in public memorial gardens because they offer "a sense of permanence" and, on a practical level, help you take a break from the stresses and rigours of everyday life. If you want to use plants to create a memorial space indoors on a balcony or window box, think about nearby seating for two which opens up the opportunity for conversation about your loved one. Image source, Emma Moore Image caption, Emma keeps Mabel's ashes next to a photograph of her tiny feet in her home If you don't have a garden, Wong suggests choosing commemorative house plants suited to warmer conditions. The peace lily, native to the rainforests of Colombia, will "grow perfectly well indoors all year round" but should be kept in warm conditions with low levels of light. candidates.evidence_text: A head teacher was dragged to his death for more than a mile trapped under the wheels of a car driven by a man who allegedly knew he was there, a jury heard Simon Richardson, 35, denies the murder of 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was struck and killed as he cycled home from work on 20 April Prosecutors claim Richardson stopped along the way, tried to dislodge the injured but still living cyclist, before driving on with Mullins remaining trapped under the wheels He also denies an alternative count of manslaughter and one of dangerous driving - relating to a police chase the following day - and is standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Philip Barnes KC, opening the case for the prosecution, told the jury that "plainly fit" Mullins was cycling from Stretford Grammar School to his home in Northwich - his usual 19-mile (30-km) commute - at 18:07 BST on Paddock Lane in Warburton, Trafford As the married father-of-two approached the junction with Dunham Road, a black Volvo XC90 drove straight through give-way signs and road markings and struck the left side of his bike

candidates.evidence_text: A police officer has admitted "nothing" was done to keep a mother and her four children safe in the hours before they were murdered in an arson attack At an inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court, PC Mike Grundy said he did not think there was a "risk of fire" at the home of Michelle Pearson and her four children in Walkden, Salford - despite Zak Bolland having made threats to "petrol bomb" the property Four of Michelle's children were murdered in the arson attack on 11 December 2017; Michelle, 37, died in August 2019, after being badly burned Bolland and David Worrall were jailed for life in 2018 for the murder of the four children, and convicted in 2021 of Michelle's murder Bolland was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 40 years, and Worrall was sentenced to life with a minimum of 37 years in jail The court previously heard Grundy and PC Gemma Quinn went to the scene in Walkden around 01:25 GMT on 11 December 2017, after Michelle called 999 because Bolland and three others were outside her house

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Council has made just under £3m from a deal to share in the so-called "super-profits" from developments built on its land by Manchester City's owners A deal struck in 2014 meant the council would receive payments if the profits made by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) on schemes in Ancoats and New Islington exceeded a certain level But Prof Adam Leaver, co-author of a 2022 report by the University of Sheffield into the council's relationship with ADUG, said commercial secrecy around the arrangements meant it was hard to know if the council got the best value it could The council said it expected another payment soon, and that the regeneration had been worth £1.25bn to the city In 2008, Manchester City was bought for £200m by ADUG, owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan - a senior member of the Abu Dhabi ruling family, who is a current vice president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) In the next decade, the club went on to win the first three of eight Premier League titles, and ADUG and Manchester City Council became partners in a company called Manchester Life

He said he ‘did not think anything of it’ until the fines came through He said he never made the mistake again but feels he has been unfairly caught out. The bus lane comes to an end just before a junction with Bellfield Avenue He later submitted a Freedom of Information request to Oldham council which showed the single camera issued 4,205 penalty charge notices and raked in £95,014 in revenue between September 2024 and August 2026. In May 2026 alone, the camera issued 290 fines generating £8,026 in 31 He said: “In both instances, I merely moved over a couple of metres before the bus lane officially ended to prepare for the merge into the general traffic lane. There was no bus present, no queue was jumped, and zero advantage was gained

Three major lines will be shut from Monday (October 19) until next month The closures are the second phase of works to ‘future proof’ the tracks around Cornbrook, Deansgate-Castlefield and Trafford Bar. Around four kilometres of rail which is coming to the end of its 30-year lifespan will be replaced, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has said The works, expected to finish by Sunday, November 1, will mean that no trams will run on the Altrincham , Eccles and Trafford Centre lines. Further disruptions will impact the East Didsbury and Manchester Airport lines, which will stop at Firswood, while the Rochdale line will st The network has been hit by a series of major works over the course of 2026, including a three-week closure on the same stretch during the summer But passengers will get a reprieve in 2027, with just one major round of work scheduled for the year, Metrolink network director Ian Davies said. That will again see the stations around Cornbrook close and is expected to take place over the Easter school holidays

Michael Joseph said the fine 'undermines the autopay system' after they were charged for dropping their son off at the airport The 52-year-old said his partner took their son to the Terminal 2 pick-up zone on September 23. candidates.evidence_text: Winter Hill fires How '4,000 holes in Blackburn, Lancashire' are protecting us against wildfires Eight years on from the devastating fires of 2018 Winter Hill is still recovering, but a huge new scheme to 'rewet' the moor hopes to prevent future disas Add to preferred sources Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 05:48, 14 Oct 2026 The rain is coming down sideways. From just a few hundred yards away the 1,000ft high TV mast is invisible in the mist Underfoot the ground is so boggy it wobbles like blancmange. Stood halfway up Winter Hill on a sodden Monday morning, it's hard to imagine this was the scene of one of the UK's worst wild fires. But back in the summer of 2018 that's exactly what it was Then conditions on the moor on the border of Bolton and Blackburn were very different. The UK was in the midst of a prolonged heatwave leaving the grass and peat parched So, when a fire was started deliberately near the mast authorities were on high alert. To make matters worse the following day a second blaze broke out on another part of the moor And when on the third day the wind changed direction and the fires joined up, it was a recipe for disaster. At the height of the blaze 150 firefighters were battling the flames as helicopters dropped hundreds of thousands of litres of water on the moors

candidates.evidence_text: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources News Dianne Bourne Lifestyle Editor 00:20, 14 Oct 2026 Updated 06:27, 14 Oct 2026 It's about as fitting as it gets that the final social media post from Councillor Pat Karney was one celebrating Manchester and Christmas , two of his greatest passions. No Relentlessly enthusiastic, and fiercely proud of his home city, he was always trying to make things better for the communities he served so tirelessly for the past 50 years As Manchester's self-appointed Christmas spokesperson, he was the man the council relied on to pull on an elf hat, the Christmas jumper, and ensure everyone was ready to celebrate - even if it was the start of November. He ensured the markets every year would get bigger and bette He was also instrumental in bringing the now annual Christmas Parade to life, after the success of the Manchester Day parade, his brainchild, was started in 2010. These events, which bring joy to thousands of people each year, are a special part of Pat's legacy But then Pat sure did love a parade - a regular at Manchester Pride, The St Patrick's Day Parade and Manchester Day. When his home patch of Harpurhey started its own parade in 2025, he hailed walking in it as "the proudest moment of my life."

It was unforgivable' Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 18:43, 13 Oct 2026 View Image Sanela Osmanovic, pictured A cruel thief pretended to befriend an 82-year-old then shoved her to the ground in a 'unforgivable' mugging. Sanela Osmanovic watched the pensioner withdraw £300 from a cash point in Moss Side before following her to a bus stop on Moss Lane East, Manchester Crown Court heard There the 44-year-old struck up conversation by asking the victim her age. When she replied saying she was born 'in 1942 during the Second World War' Osmanovic said: "I can't believe it. You look 65 to 70." The victim then hugged Osmanovic and told her she was kind, only for the thief to push her to the floor and steal her handbag containing the money and an iPhone. She was later seen on CCTV carrying the bag and arrested The victim was taken to hospital, where she was found to have a fractured spine, although medics were unable to ascertain if the injury had been sustained in the attack on April 17 last year. In a victim impact statement the woman said the assault meant her quality of life had 'c The court heard Osmanovic, a long-term drug addict, had 50 previous convictions for 105 offences dating back to 2001, including 57 for theft-related crimes. Steve Nikolich, defending, said Osmanovic, who the court heard was born in Serbia and had fled the Balkan wars as a child

candidates.lead: Heaton Park Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C.
candidates.evidence_text: Heaton Park Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled Statements have been issued Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 18:20, 13 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Fontaines D.C. (Image: Kenny Brown) A Jewish council has called for gigs at Heaton Park by Irish rock band Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled. The Jewish Representative Council of Greater Manchester and Region, in a statement on Tuesday, said it had 'concerns' over 'the potential consequences of inflammatory rhetoric f The Heaton Park shows - on July 3 and 4 next year - were announced last month. Fontaines D.C. also announced shows in Cardiff, Newcastle, Glasgow and London as part of a UK headline tour, and are set to be supported by Little Simz and Viagra Boys The band has expressed its support for Palestine at previous shows. Pictures show the phrases 'free Palestine' and 'Israel is committing genocide' appearing on screens during a gig by the band in London last year The JRC said it had 'registered [its] profound concerns' with Manchester council over the Heaton Park shows. The statement said it expected 'robust and adequate safeguards' to be in place 'to protect the Jewish community' In response, the council said addressing any concerns from the Jewish community would be 'front and centre in preparations for these events'

'Dangerous' Adam Wass barricaded himself in a terrified stranger's house after twice pulling the trigger of a firearm in Salford He has now been locked up for six years. The 36-year-old, Greater Manchester Police said, put two innocent people through 'terrifying ordeals' Wass attempted to shoot at a woman on St Joseph's Drive, Ordsall, on February 1 this year. The weapon misfired and no bullet emerged from the chamber Wass pulled the trigger again as the woman ran and took cover behind a car. That time, a bullet was fired. GMP said Wass then went into a nearby home and threatened a man inside, who fled unhurt Armed officers were scrambled at around 8.15pm. Wass, who still had the gun, barricaded himself inside and refused to give himself up

It has emerged the major procedural error occurred in the authority’s handling of a Rowland Homes appeal on a Bolton council planning ref The town hall said the issue was due to a ‘coding error’ in generating the letters and has issued an apology to all affected residents In March this year the council’s planning committee threw out the plans after hearing fears the development could have ‘merged Bolton and Bury ’ Concerns about local biodiversity, traffic issues, and ‘green belt’ vs ‘grey belt’ land were central to the refusal, with the council deciding that the benefits of 80 extra houses did not outweigh the potential negatives An appeal against that decision was lodged by Rowland Homes and the case is set to be heard by the Planning inspectorate in the coming months

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Builder says 'it's a trap' as one Oldham bus lane camera hits him with double fine - with 4,200 others affected The Oldham camera issued over 4,000 fines between September 2024 and August 2026 Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barne A builder fears an Oldham bus lane camera is becoming a ‘revenue trap’ after he discovered thousands have been fined Chris Bagnall, a builder from Stoke-on-Trent, was driving along Ashton Road on the way to work in Oldham when he was hit by two fines for going into the end of a bus lane . He said he ‘did not think anything of it’ until the fines came through He said he never made the mistake again but feels he has been unfairly caught out. The bus lane comes to an end just before a junction with Bellfield Avenue He later submitted a Freedom of Information request to Oldham council which showed the single camera issued 4,205 penalty charge notices and raked in £95,014 in revenue between September 2024 and August 2026. In May 2026 alone, the camera issued 290 fines generating £8,026 in 31 He said: “In both instances, I merely moved over a couple of metres before the bus lane officially ended to prepare for the merge into the general traffic lane. There was no bus present, no queue was jumped, and zero advantage was gained

candidates.evidence_text: Metrolink Hope for Metrolink commuters as bosses reveal 2027 tram closure plans The comments come as passengers brace for two more weeks of travel chaos from Monday Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:10, 14 Oct 2026 View 2 Ima Just one round of major tram works are on the cards for next year, transport bosses have promised. It comes as commuters brace themselves for two more weeks of travel chaos. Three major lines will be shut from Monday (October 19) until next month The closures are the second phase of works to ‘future proof’ the tracks around Cornbrook, Deansgate-Castlefield and Trafford Bar. Around four kilometres of rail which is coming to the end of its 30-year lifespan will be replaced, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has said The works, expected to finish by Sunday, November 1, will mean that no trams will run on the Altrincham , Eccles and Trafford Centre lines. Further disruptions will impact the East Didsbury and Manchester Airport lines, which will stop at Firswood, while the Rochdale line will st The network has been hit by a series of major works over the course of 2026, including a three-week closure on the same stretch during the summer But passengers will get a reprieve in 2027, with just one major round of work scheduled for the year, Metrolink network director Ian Davies said. That will again see the stations around Cornbrook close and is expected to take place over the Easter school holidays

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule' He has hit out at the autopay system at Manchester Airport, but they have defended the fine Add to preferred s A man has slammed Manchester Airport after his wife was issued a £100 fine - despite their car being registered for automatic payments at drop-off zones. Michael Joseph said the fine 'undermines the autopay system' after they were charged for dropping their son off at the airport The 52-year-old said his partner took their son to the Terminal 2 pick-up zone on September 23. The family, from Salford , previously set up autopay after having 'a bad experience with parking at the airport' The system allows people to register their vehicle online with a payment card and be automatically charged for pick-ups or drop-offs at the airport If drivers don't have autopay set up, they have to visit Manchester Airport's website - or call up - to pay charges by midnight the day after visits. Missing the payment deadline results in a £100 Parking Charge Notice View 4 Images They received the fine despite having an AutoPay account (Image: Manchester Evening News)

candidates.lead: Winter Hill fires How '4,000 holes in Blackburn, Lancashire' are protecting us against wildfires Eight years on from the devastating fires of 2018 Winter Hill is still recovering, but a huge new scheme to 'rewet' the moor hopes to prevent future disas Add to preferred sources Com
candidates.evidence_text: Winter Hill fires How '4,000 holes in Blackburn, Lancashire' are protecting us against wildfires Eight years on from the devastating fires of 2018 Winter Hill is still recovering, but a huge new scheme to 'rewet' the moor hopes to prevent future disas Add to preferred sources Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 05:48, 14 Oct 2026 The rain is coming down sideways. From just a few hundred yards away the 1,000ft high TV mast is invisible in the mist Underfoot the ground is so boggy it wobbles like blancmange. Stood halfway up Winter Hill on a sodden Monday morning, it's hard to imagine this was the scene of one of the UK's worst wild fires. But back in the summer of 2018 that's exactly what it was Then conditions on the moor on the border of Bolton and Blackburn were very different. The UK was in the midst of a prolonged heatwave leaving the grass and peat parched So, when a fire was started deliberately near the mast authorities were on high alert. To make matters worse the following day a second blaze broke out on another part of the moor And when on the third day the wind changed direction and the fires joined up, it was a recipe for disaster. At the height of the blaze 150 firefighters were battling the flames as helicopters dropped hundreds of thousands of litres of water on the moors

candidates.lead: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources New
candidates.evidence_text: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources News Dianne Bourne Lifestyle Editor 00:20, 14 Oct 2026 Updated 06:27, 14 Oct 2026 It's about as fitting as it gets that the final social media post from Councillor Pat Karney was one celebrating Manchester and Christmas , two of his greatest passions. No Relentlessly enthusiastic, and fiercely proud of his home city, he was always trying to make things better for the communities he served so tirelessly for the past 50 years As Manchester's self-appointed Christmas spokesperson, he was the man the council relied on to pull on an elf hat, the Christmas jumper, and ensure everyone was ready to celebrate - even if it was the start of November. He ensured the markets every year would get bigger and bette He was also instrumental in bringing the now annual Christmas Parade to life, after the success of the Manchester Day parade, his brainchild, was started in 2010. These events, which bring joy to thousands of people each year, are a special part of Pat's legacy But then Pat sure did love a parade - a regular at Manchester Pride, The St Patrick's Day Parade and Manchester Day. When his home patch of Harpurhey started its own parade in 2025, he hailed walking in it as "the proudest moment of my life."

Sanela Osmanovic watched the pensioner withdraw £300 from a cash point in Moss Side before following her to a bus stop on Moss Lane East, Manchester Crown Court heard There the 44-year-old struck up conversation by asking the victim her age. When she replied saying she was born 'in 1942 during the Second World War' Osmanovic said: "I can't believe it. You look 65 to 70." The victim then hugged Osmanovic and told her she was kind, only for the thief to push her to the floor and steal her handbag containing the money and an iPhone. candidates.lead: Heaton Park Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C.
candidates.evidence_text: Heaton Park Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled Statements have been issued Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 18:20, 13 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Fontaines D.C. (Image: Kenny Brown) A Jewish council has called for gigs at Heaton Park by Irish rock band Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled. The Jewish Representative Council of Greater Manchester and Region, in a statement on Tuesday, said it had 'concerns' over 'the potential consequences of inflammatory rhetoric f The Heaton Park shows - on July 3 and 4 next year - were announced last month. Fontaines D.C. also announced shows in Cardiff, Newcastle, Glasgow and London as part of a UK headline tour, and are set to be supported by Little Simz and Viagra Boys The band has expressed its support for Palestine at previous shows. Pictures show the phrases 'free Palestine' and 'Israel is committing genocide' appearing on screens during a gig by the band in London last year The JRC said it had 'registered [its] profound concerns' with Manchester council over the Heaton Park shows. The statement said it expected 'robust and adequate safeguards' to be in place 'to protect the Jewish community' In response, the council said addressing any concerns from the Jewish community would be 'front and centre in preparations for these events'

candidates.evidence_text: Crime Gunman shot at woman before barricading himself in stranger's house in four-hour stand-off with armed police Adam Wass has been jailed Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 18:05, 13 Oct 2026 View 4 Images Adam Wass, 3 A gunman who shot at a woman before a four-hour standoff with armed police has been jailed. 'Dangerous' Adam Wass barricaded himself in a terrified stranger's house after twice pulling the trigger of a firearm in Salford He has now been locked up for six years. The 36-year-old, Greater Manchester Police said, put two innocent people through 'terrifying ordeals' Wass attempted to shoot at a woman on St Joseph's Drive, Ordsall, on February 1 this year. The weapon misfired and no bullet emerged from the chamber Wass pulled the trigger again as the woman ran and took cover behind a car. That time, a bullet was fired. GMP said Wass then went into a nearby home and threatened a man inside, who fled unhurt Armed officers were scrambled at around 8.15pm. Wass, who still had the gun, barricaded himself inside and refused to give himself up

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton councillor switches allegiance just 10 weeks after being elected New Green councillor Yusuf Davda said his decision had not been 'taken lightly or out of frustration with others' Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local dem A Bolton councillor who was elected 10 weeks ago has switched allegiance and joined the Green Party. Coun Yusuf Davda recently topped the poll in a by-election for Rumworth ward on July 30 as an Independent He gained 1.458 votes with Labour in second on 1,054. The Greens were third in the poll, with their candidate Alan Johnson getting 517 votes Coun Davda said: “Over recent months, it has become increasingly clear to me that real, positive change for our neighbourhoods requires a fresh approach and a political home that puts fairness, community action, and the local environment at the heart of everything “Joining the Green Party is not a decision taken lightly or out of frustration with others, but out of a genuine belief that it offers the most constructive and community-focused path forward “My focus on the ground will not change, I will continue to work tirelessly for our residents every single day, and I remain committed to working collaboratively with colleagues across all parties for the good of Bolton .”

candidates.lead: Bolton Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans The authority blamed a 'coding error' for the blunder and has apologised Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17 Bolton council sent out lett
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans The authority blamed a 'coding error' for the blunder and has apologised Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17 Bolton council sent out letters to residents incorrectly telling them they could not object to controversial housing plans on green belt land. It has emerged the major procedural error occurred in the authority’s handling of a Rowland Homes appeal on a Bolton council planning ref The town hall said the issue was due to a ‘coding error’ in generating the letters and has issued an apology to all affected residents In March this year the council’s planning committee threw out the plans after hearing fears the development could have ‘merged Bolton and Bury ’ Concerns about local biodiversity, traffic issues, and ‘green belt’ vs ‘grey belt’ land were central to the refusal, with the council deciding that the benefits of 80 extra houses did not outweigh the potential negatives An appeal against that decision was lodged by Rowland Homes and the case is set to be heard by the Planning inspectorate in the coming months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Altrincham An end to Altrincham's 20-year development saga could be in sight Plans for the site have ranged from a hospital to a bowling alley Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:14, 13 Oct 2026 View Image Land off Oakfield Roa Trafford council is pushing forward with plans to develop an Altrincham site that has stalled since 2007 Two competing visions are set to be considered by the council’s cabinet next week for the 4.5-acre site off Oakfield Road, previously known as Altair. One would be a residential-led scheme A spokeswoman said more than 100 new homes could be built there, if that approach is taken forward. Plan two could see a retail-led approach taken, with this most likely to include a large food store or supermarket Council documents indicate a preference for the former approach to be taken forwards. If that is the case, some ground-floor retail uses could also be incorporated, they add The land, near Altrincham Interchange, currently comprises the Planet Ice ice rink and around 320 parking spaces. Trafford council said the parking is important for the neighbouring Move Altrincham leisure site

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher knowingly dragged him under car for more than a mile after hitting him as he cycled home, trial told Simon Richardson denies murdering Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walk The man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins knowingly dragged the popular educator under his car for more than a mile after hitting him as he cycled home, a trial has been told Simon Richardson hit Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham in April, a court heard. The 56-year-old head was making his way home to Northwich, Cheshire, after work when he was struck at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, a jury was told He was dragged under the wheels of the car for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm, a court was told Mr Richardson, 35, earlier failed to properly observe a junction, 'flying straight through the give way markers', before hitting Mr Mullins, the court heard The defendant didn't stop and 'put his foot down', prosecutors alleged as a murder trial began on Tuesday (October 13). Mr Mullins was trapped under the car, the court heard, while his damaged bike was left in the road

Voters elected 13 new Reform councillors bringing their total number to 16 The leadership election was kickstarted after Failsworth West councillor Mark Wilkinson stood down citing health reasons . Coun Wilkinson himself had recently been elected to replace Royton councillor Lewis Quigg Coun Taylor’s appointment as leader comes at a crucial time. Next month, Reform will be looking to defend Failsworth West in a by-election and the party will be looking to make further gains in 2027’s local elections in an effort to become Oldham’s largest political party The Waterhead councillor was previously stood as a candidate for the Brexit Party as well as the independent Northern Heart Party, which he still leads according to the Electoral Commission’s website. Reform have told the LDRS he is now resigning from this position

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Builder says 'it's a trap' as one Oldham bus lane camera hits him with double fine - with 4,200 others affected The Oldham camera issued over 4,000 fines between September 2024 and August 2026 Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barne A builder fears an Oldham bus lane camera is becoming a ‘revenue trap’ after he discovered thousands have been fined Chris Bagnall, a builder from Stoke-on-Trent, was driving along Ashton Road on the way to work in Oldham when he was hit by two fines for going into the end of a bus lane . He said he ‘did not think anything of it’ until the fines came through He said he never made the mistake again but feels he has been unfairly caught out. The bus lane comes to an end just before a junction with Bellfield Avenue He later submitted a Freedom of Information request to Oldham council which showed the single camera issued 4,205 penalty charge notices and raked in £95,014 in revenue between September 2024 and August 2026. In May 2026 alone, the camera issued 290 fines generating £8,026 in 31 He said: “In both instances, I merely moved over a couple of metres before the bus lane officially ended to prepare for the merge into the general traffic lane. There was no bus present, no queue was jumped, and zero advantage was gained

candidates.summary: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources New

candidates.lead: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources New
candidates.evidence_text: Councillor Pat Karney Mr Christmas and Manchester's constant cheerleader - farewell to a city legend as Pat Karney dies aged 78 Following the death of Pat Karney, Dianne Bourne remembers two sides of a Manchester legend - the radical 80s politician wh Add to preferred sources News Dianne Bourne Lifestyle Editor 00:20, 14 Oct 2026 Updated 06:27, 14 Oct 2026 It's about as fitting as it gets that the final social media post from Councillor Pat Karney was one celebrating Manchester and Christmas , two of his greatest passions. No Relentlessly enthusiastic, and fiercely proud of his home city, he was always trying to make things better for the communities he served so tirelessly for the past 50 years As Manchester's self-appointed Christmas spokesperson, he was the man the council relied on to pull on an elf hat, the Christmas jumper, and ensure everyone was ready to celebrate - even if it was the start of November. He ensured the markets every year would get bigger and bette He was also instrumental in bringing the now annual Christmas Parade to life, after the success of the Manchester Day parade, his brainchild, was started in 2010. These events, which bring joy to thousands of people each year, are a special part of Pat's legacy But then Pat sure did love a parade - a regular at Manchester Pride, The St Patrick's Day Parade and Manchester Day. When his home patch of Harpurhey started its own parade in 2025, he hailed walking in it as "the proudest moment of my life."

candidates.evidence_text: Metrolink Hope for Metrolink commuters as bosses reveal 2027 tram closure plans The comments come as passengers brace for two more weeks of travel chaos from Monday Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:10, 14 Oct 2026 View 2 Ima Just one round of major tram works are on the cards for next year, transport bosses have promised. It comes as commuters brace themselves for two more weeks of travel chaos. Three major lines will be shut from Monday (October 19) until next month The closures are the second phase of works to ‘future proof’ the tracks around Cornbrook, Deansgate-Castlefield and Trafford Bar. Around four kilometres of rail which is coming to the end of its 30-year lifespan will be replaced, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has said The works, expected to finish by Sunday, November 1, will mean that no trams will run on the Altrincham , Eccles and Trafford Centre lines. Further disruptions will impact the East Didsbury and Manchester Airport lines, which will stop at Firswood, while the Rochdale line will st The network has been hit by a series of major works over the course of 2026, including a three-week closure on the same stretch during the summer But passengers will get a reprieve in 2027, with just one major round of work scheduled for the year, Metrolink network director Ian Davies said. That will again see the stations around Cornbrook close and is expected to take place over the Easter school holidays

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule' He has hit out at the autopay system at Manchester Airport, but they have defended the fine Add to preferred s A man has slammed Manchester Airport after his wife was issued a £100 fine - despite their car being registered for automatic payments at drop-off zones. Michael Joseph said the fine 'undermines the autopay system' after they were charged for dropping their son off at the airport The 52-year-old said his partner took their son to the Terminal 2 pick-up zone on September 23. english_fact_card.who_affected: The family from Salford, and potentially other drivers using the airport's autopay system.
english_fact_card.why_now: The man is publicly criticising the autopay system, claiming the fine undermines it, while the airport defends the fine.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Drivers using Manchester Airport's autopay should be aware that fines can still be issued if payment deadlines are missed.
english_fact_card.reader_action: If using autopay, ensure your vehicle is correctly registered and payments are processed; otherwise pay by midnight the day after your visit to avoid a £100 Parking Charge Notice.

candidates.evidence_text: Winter Hill fires How '4,000 holes in Blackburn, Lancashire' are protecting us against wildfires Eight years on from the devastating fires of 2018 Winter Hill is still recovering, but a huge new scheme to 'rewet' the moor hopes to prevent future disas Add to preferred sources Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 05:48, 14 Oct 2026 The rain is coming down sideways. From just a few hundred yards away the 1,000ft high TV mast is invisible in the mist Underfoot the ground is so boggy it wobbles like blancmange. Stood halfway up Winter Hill on a sodden Monday morning, it's hard to imagine this was the scene of one of the UK's worst wild fires. But back in the summer of 2018 that's exactly what it was Then conditions on the moor on the border of Bolton and Blackburn were very different. The UK was in the midst of a prolonged heatwave leaving the grass and peat parched So, when a fire was started deliberately near the mast authorities were on high alert. To make matters worse the following day a second blaze broke out on another part of the moor And when on the third day the wind changed direction and the fires joined up, it was a recipe for disaster. At the height of the blaze 150 firefighters were battling the flames as helicopters dropped hundreds of thousands of litres of water on the moors

candidates.evidence_text: Salford 'HMO' targeted in latest Salford window and graffiti attack is actually a family home Police have issued a statement Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 18:26, 13 Oct 2026 View 3 Images The house targeted (Image: Sean An 'HMO' targeted in a criminal damage attack is actually a family home, the Manchester Evening News understands. The property was vandalised and damaged against a backdrop of similar targeted attacks across Salford on 'houses of multiple occupation' A front window was smashed at the house in Little Hulton on Monday night (October 12), with red spray paint also daubed onto its white front door and a window Posts on social media uploaded after the attack included photographs and claimed it was 'another HMO'. But the Manchester Evening News understands it is a family home. Images showed a hatchback car parked on the driveway Police have confirmed an investigation is underway. In a statement, Greater Manchester Police said: "We were called to a report of criminal damage at 8.53pm. Enquiries are ongoing." Official sources have told the Manchester Evening News it's not an HMO. No injuries have been reported, but it's not known whether anyone was inside the house at the time

candidates.evidence_text: Heaton Park Jewish leaders call for Heaton Park gigs by Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled Statements have been issued Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 18:20, 13 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Fontaines D.C. (Image: Kenny Brown) A Jewish council has called for gigs at Heaton Park by Irish rock band Fontaines D.C. to be cancelled. The Jewish Representative Council of Greater Manchester and Region, in a statement on Tuesday, said it had 'concerns' over 'the potential consequences of inflammatory rhetoric f The Heaton Park shows - on July 3 and 4 next year - were announced last month. Fontaines D.C. also announced shows in Cardiff, Newcastle, Glasgow and London as part of a UK headline tour, and are set to be supported by Little Simz and Viagra Boys The band has expressed its support for Palestine at previous shows. Pictures show the phrases 'free Palestine' and 'Israel is committing genocide' appearing on screens during a gig by the band in London last year The JRC said it had 'registered [its] profound concerns' with Manchester council over the Heaton Park shows. The statement said it expected 'robust and adequate safeguards' to be in place 'to protect the Jewish community' In response, the council said addressing any concerns from the Jewish community would be 'front and centre in preparations for these events'

candidates.evidence_text: Crime Gunman shot at woman before barricading himself in stranger's house in four-hour stand-off with armed police Adam Wass has been jailed Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 18:05, 13 Oct 2026 View 4 Images Adam Wass, 3 A gunman who shot at a woman before a four-hour standoff with armed police has been jailed. 'Dangerous' Adam Wass barricaded himself in a terrified stranger's house after twice pulling the trigger of a firearm in Salford He has now been locked up for six years. The 36-year-old, Greater Manchester Police said, put two innocent people through 'terrifying ordeals' Wass attempted to shoot at a woman on St Joseph's Drive, Ordsall, on February 1 this year. The weapon misfired and no bullet emerged from the chamber Wass pulled the trigger again as the woman ran and took cover behind a car. That time, a bullet was fired. GMP said Wass then went into a nearby home and threatened a man inside, who fled unhurt Armed officers were scrambled at around 8.15pm. Wass, who still had the gun, barricaded himself inside and refused to give himself up

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans The authority blamed a 'coding error' for the blunder and has apologised Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17 Bolton council sent out letters to residents incorrectly telling them they could not object to controversial housing plans on green belt land. It has emerged the major procedural error occurred in the authority’s handling of a Rowland Homes appeal on a Bolton council planning ref The town hall said the issue was due to a ‘coding error’ in generating the letters and has issued an apology to all affected residents In March this year the council’s planning committee threw out the plans after hearing fears the development could have ‘merged Bolton and Bury ’ Concerns about local biodiversity, traffic issues, and ‘green belt’ vs ‘grey belt’ land were central to the refusal, with the council deciding that the benefits of 80 extra houses did not outweigh the potential negatives An appeal against that decision was lodged by Rowland Homes and the case is set to be heard by the Planning inspectorate in the coming months

evidence_texts: Bolton Bolton council wrongly told neighbours they couldn't object to 80-home green belt estate plans The authority blamed a 'coding error' for the blunder and has apologised Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 17 Bolton council sent out letters to residents incorrectly telling them they could not object to controversial housing plans on green belt land. It has emerged the major procedural error occurred in the authority’s handling of a Rowland Homes appeal on a Bolton council planning ref The town hall said the issue was due to a ‘coding error’ in generating the letters and has issued an apology to all affected residents In March this year the council’s planning committee threw out the plans after hearing fears the development could have ‘merged Bolton and Bury ’ Concerns about local biodiversity, traffic issues, and ‘green belt’ vs ‘grey belt’ land

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton councillor switches allegiance just 10 weeks after being elected New Green councillor Yusuf Davda said his decision had not been 'taken lightly or out of frustration with others' Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local dem A Bolton councillor who was elected 10 weeks ago has switched allegiance and joined the Green Party. Coun Yusuf Davda recently topped the poll in a by-election for Rumworth ward on July 30 as an Independent He gained 1.458 votes with Labour in second on 1,054. The Greens were third in the poll, with their candidate Alan Johnson getting 517 votes Coun Davda said: “Over recent months, it has become increasingly clear to me that real, positive change for our neighbourhoods requires a fresh approach and a political home that puts fairness, community action, and the local environment at the heart of everything “Joining the Green Party is not a decision taken lightly or out of frustration with others, but out of a genuine belief that it offers the most constructive and community-focused path forward “My focus on the ground will not change, I will continue to work tirelessly for our residents every single day, and I remain committed to working collaboratively with colleagues across all parties for the good of Bolton .”

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher knowingly dragged him under car for more than a mile after hitting him as he cycled home, trial told Simon Richardson denies murdering Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walk The man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins knowingly dragged the popular educator under his car for more than a mile after hitting him as he cycled home, a trial has been told Simon Richardson hit Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham in April, a court heard. The 56-year-old head was making his way home to Northwich, Cheshire, after work when he was struck at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, a jury was told He was dragged under the wheels of the car for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm, a court was told Mr Richardson, 35, earlier failed to properly observe a junction, 'flying straight through the give way markers', before hitting Mr Mullins, the court heard The defendant didn't stop and 'put his foot down', prosecutors alleged as a murder trial began on Tuesday (October 13). Mr Mullins was trapped under the car, the court heard, while his damaged bike was left in the road

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Oldham Reform UK party has a new leader as he's made a promise Coun Taylor said his election ‘comes at a critical moment’, Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 14:04, 13 Oct 2026 Updated 16:29, 13 Oct 20 Oldham Reform’s new leader said he plans to ‘save Oldham’ following a ‘close’ election to the post Waterhead councillor Paul Taylor will now take over as Reform UK’s third leader in Oldham since the local elections in May this year. Voters elected 13 new Reform councillors bringing their total number to 16 The leadership election was kickstarted after Failsworth West councillor Mark Wilkinson stood down citing health reasons . Coun Wilkinson himself had recently been elected to replace Royton councillor Lewis Quigg Coun Taylor’s appointment as leader comes at a crucial time. Next month, Reform will be looking to defend Failsworth West in a by-election and the party will be looking to make further gains in 2027’s local elections in an effort to become Oldham’s largest political party The Waterhead councillor was previously stood as a candidate for the Brexit Party as well as the independent Northern Heart Party, which he still leads according to the Electoral Commission’s website. Reform have told the LDRS he is now resigning from this position

Residents on the stretch of Hollins Road near the junction of Hogwill Crescent, woke early last Friday morning to find it looking like a 'lake' with the water waist- Locals said a blocked pipe led to flooding which affected at least six properties Five fire engines were scrambled and spent nine hours at the scene. They helped at least one family's children to get out of their property through bedroom windows and down a ladder Some of those whose homes were damaged by the 'contaminated' water had to be put up in hotels by the council. The water had largely subsided by the following day, but the road has been closed between Lynmouth Avenue and Crofton Street since View 5 Images United Utilities say investigations into the flooding are ongoing (Image: Manchester Evening News)

candidates.evidence_text: 3DReid is the scheme architect. Credit: via Citypress The redevelopment of the former Greater Manchester Police headquarters off Chester Road has been beefed up with an additional 200 homes and could be on site this time next year A report to Trafford Council’s executive states that completion of the 1,400-home scheme is expected before the end of 2034. Before that, a great deal has to happen Firstly, a planning application for the project, which FEC was instructed to lead back in 2021, is expected this month. It will feature some 200 more homes than outlined during the last round of consultation, when the plan was for 1,200 FEC is also committed to delivering 25% affordable homes on site despite constrained viability The Trafford report states that a viability appraisal for the scheme is showing a 5% developer’s profit against an expectation of 15%. As a result, public sector funding support is likely to be required to deliver the project

candidates.evidence_text: A young fundraiser from Denton has hiked up the highest mountain in Wales to raise funds for homelessness charity Emmaus Mossley On Saturday 19 September, seven-year-old Freddie and his family successfully completed their sponsored walk up Snowdon. Freddie wanted to do a challenge to help people affected by homelessness and has so far raised more than £1,100 for Emmaus Mossley Freddie commented: “I really enjoyed doing Snowden, especially all the climbing. It was easy and I want to do another big mountain next year. It makes me sad to see homeless people and I wanted to help in any way I could.” Prior to the walk, Freddie visited Emmaus Mossley, a local charity that helps to empower people to overcome homelessness for good. Whilst resident at Emmaus, each person is supported to build their confidence, self-esteem, skills and work experience to achieve their goals Freddie’s mum, Kirsty, added: “The weather was awful but we did it and it was all for a great cause. Freddie was amazing – he was in front helping everyone along and he can’t wait to do the next one.” Emmaus Mossley’s residential community provides a home and tailored support for up to 26 people at any one time. Funds raised from Freddie’s challenge will go towards the charity’s plans to improve the community building and facilities

Whilst resident at Emmaus, each person is supported to build their confidence, self-esteem, skills and work experience to achieve their goals Freddie’s mum, Kirsty, added: “The weather was awful but we did it and it was all for a great cause. Freddie was amazing – he was in front helping everyone along and he can’t wait to do the next one.” Emmaus Mossley’s residential community provides a home and tailored support for up to 26 people at any one time. candidates.evidence_text: How one city became the centre of a social media circus In the aftermath of heavy rain, on a quiet street in East Salford, a woman is hurrying towards a terraced house. A little boy grasps her hand, smiling, breaking into sporadic skips as he tries to keep pace. Shards of glass litter the road and numerous windows have been covered wi This unassuming pair live in one of the five houses targeted on this street last week in a supposed attack on Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs). But the woman – who is black, in her 30s, and declines to give her name for obvious reasons – tells me that her house is not an HMO This woman and her neighbours were not the first people to be caught up in what has been described on social media as a “protest” against these kinds of properties. Any house or flat that’s rented out by three or more tenants – at least two of whom are unrelated – and where they Last week’s attacks have divided Salford, prompting public outrage, as well as praise, across social media. Facebook, Instagram and TikTok have grown rife with videos titled things like “SALFORD ERUPTS”. Much of the social media coverage on self-styled citizen journalist channels One image in particular, the words “No HMOs” scrawled across a boarded-up window, has been shared widely across social and mainstream media alike. While this message – daubed in black paint – was unambiguous, it seems the facts behind it are considerably less so

candidates.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

The internal document – that will be shared with council workers tomorrow and is based on a survey of nearly 1,200 staff – The report describes a culture at the council in which senior staff can act inappropriately with seeming impunity. Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

candidates.evidence_text: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred vans, and the doors swing open. Out from within comes cart after cart full of corn This is the not-entirely-secret HQ of the Market Street corn vendors: a four-storey council-owned car park, sitting across two of Manchester’s busiest streets. When I get there, the men are working in silence, hands sheathed in black gloves, bags of sweetcorn torn open, cardboard Just as I’m about to approach a vendor, I’m forwarded an email from a reader. It has the subject line The Mystery We All Want Solved "The reason I’m writing is because the people of Manchester are desperate to know what the hell is going on with all of the corn sellers on Market St "Why are there now so many of them? How on earth do they make a profit? Are they independent vendors or all part of the same company? Is their presence legal? What does their proliferation say about the state of the city centre?”

candidates.evidence_text: Right at Home South Trafford and Wyncourt Nursing Home staged a joint picnic at Wyncourt Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Two Outstanding-rated Timperley care providers have joined forces for the first time to raise money for dementia Right at Home South Trafford and Wyncourt Nursing Home staged a joint picnic at Wyncourt this summer in aid of Dementia Adventure, Right at Home’s charity partner. Absolutely fantastic,” says Vicki Hobson-Middleton, activities coordinator at Wyncourt Wyncourt’s garden was dressed for the occasion, with balloons, tombola, bingo, noughts and crosses and ring toss. Family members donated cakes, the home’s chef made more, and there were sandwiches on the tables. Relatives came over, staff joined in and the weather held “Everybody got involved,” Vicki says. “I was really worried about the weather, but it was just absolutely stunning.”

candidates.evidence_text: It's one of the longest-running sagas in the town Share on WhatsApp Share via Email One of Altrincham's longest-running regeneration sagas could be entering a new chapter, with Trafford Council proposing to turn the former Altair site into a major residential development The council is recommending that the 4.5-acre site between Oakfield Road and Moss Lane should be developed primarily for housing, potentially bringing an end to almost two decades of failed plans for a major new shopping, leisure and residential quarter The proposals, which will be considered by Trafford Council's Executive on Monday October 19, would also see the existing surface car park potentially replaced by a multi-storey parking and transport hub An indicative masterplan includes apartment buildings of five storeys or more, smaller residential blocks, commercial space and landscaped communal areas The plans represent a significant change of direction for the site, which was originally earmarked for the £70 million Altair development first unveiled in 2008

candidates.evidence_text: They said they were "deeply saddened" by the decision to adopt the motion Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Altrincham's Green councillors Dan Jerrome, Geraldine Coggins and Michael Welton Green councillors in Trafford have publicly distanced themselves from their national party's controversial new policy on Zionism, warning that it could negatively af In a strongly worded statement, seven Green councillors, including representatives of Altrincham, said they were "deeply saddened" by the decision to adopt the motion at the party's national conference on Sunday The motion, entitled Zionism is Racism , was passed by 1,022 votes to 813 at the Green Party conference in Brighton It formally establishes the Greens as an anti-Zionist party, defines Zionism as a form of racism and supports the creation of a single democratic Palestinian state across historic Palestine, with Jerusalem as its capital But Trafford's Green councillors have made clear they oppose aspects of the policy, particularly its position on Palestinian statehood and its definition of Zionism

candidates.evidence_text: North Cestrian School is expanding into the former Loreto Preparatory School site Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Plans to create up to 300 additional secondary school places in Altrincham have taken a significant step forward with the appointment of a contractor to oversee the next phase of the project Trafford Council has appointed construction firm Tilbury Douglas to work on the proposed expansion of North Cestrian School into the former Loreto Preparatory School site The council announced in August that it had purchased the neighbouring site, paving the way for the school to expand and help meet growing demand for secondary school places in the area Tilbury Douglas has now been appointed under a Pre-Construction Services Agreement (PCSA), which will see the company work with Trafford Council, Hamblin Education Trust and the design team to develop the scheme ahead of the construction phase The proposed expansion would allow North Cestrian to accommodate up to 300 additional pupils, helping more Altrincham children secure places at a local secondary school

candidates.evidence_text: The Altrincham line will be closed again between Monday October 19 and Sunday November 1 Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Transport for Greater Manchester has announced a major change to its plans for the upcoming Altrincham Metrolink closure , with direct shuttle buses now set to operate between Altrincham and Manchester city centre The move comes after TfGM initially confirmed that no dedicated replacement buses would serve Altrincham, Navigation Road or Timperley during the two-week shutdown from Monday October 19 to Sunday November 1 Instead, passengers were told to use the existing 263 bus service or trains into Manchester, with replacement buses operating only between Sale and the city centre But in a welcome change of plan, TfGM has now confirmed that a new non-stop shuttle service will run directly between Altrincham and Piccadilly every 15 minutes The service will operate between 7am and 7pm during the closure, although a detailed timetable has yet to be published

candidates.summary: Simon Richardson, 35, denies the murder of 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was struck and killed as he cycled home from work on 20 April Prosecutors claim Richardson stopped along the way, tried to dislodge the injured but still living cyclist, before driving on with Mullins rem

candidates.evidence_text: Simon Richardson, 35, denies the murder of 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was struck and killed as he cycled home from work on 20 April Prosecutors claim Richardson stopped along the way, tried to dislodge the injured but still living cyclist, before driving on with Mullins remaining trapped under the wheels He also denies an alternative count of manslaughter and one of dangerous driving - relating to a police chase the following day - and is standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Philip Barnes KC, opening the case for the prosecution, told the jury that "plainly fit" Mullins was cycling from Stretford Grammar School to his home in Northwich - his usual 19-mile (30-km) commute - at 18:07 BST on Paddock Lane in Warburton, Trafford As the married father-of-two approached the junction with Dunham Road, a black Volvo XC90 drove straight through give-way signs and road markings and struck the left side of his bike Barnes said Richardson, of no fixed address, did not stop and instead fled the scene towards Cheshire hitting speeds above 60mph
