Passengers travelling across Manchester's tram network were in for a surprise today (Friday 9 October) as 6,000 free books were given away on the city's trams by Read Manchester to mark World Mental Health which falls on Saturday.. The free book giveaway in partnership with Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) saw thousands of free reads placed on tram seats at the crack of dawn this morning - a book on every seat - and sent on their way from tram depots right across the tram network, ready to be picked up by passengers of all ages.. . The good read giveaway is part of Read Manchester's Take 10 to Read campaign which was first launched by Read Manchester in 2018 and is now promoted by the National Literacy Trust across the UK - and also this year worldwide through a world record attempt.. . The campaign highlights the wellbeing benefits of reading, and each year encourages people of all ages to spend 10 minutes reading on and around World Mental Health Day (10 October). to help improve their mental health.. . It complements wider work around the city by Read Manchester to encourage reading for enjoyment and help people discover the positive impact reading can have on learning, wellbeing and everyday life.. . This year's Take Ten to Read campaign, taking place during the National Year of Reading 2026, calls on people to explore their hobbies and interests through reading, with a simple message: whatever you're into, take 10 and read into it.. . Councillor Shazia Butt, Executive Member for Culture, Libraries and Leisure, Manchester City Council, said: . . "Good mental health is important for everyone whatever your age and escaping into the world of a book and reading - even just for ten minutes a day - is something that research shows can make a positive difference to how people feel.. . "Together with our partners at the National Literacy Trust we've been helping Mancunians and others find a love of books and reading for ten years now through Read Manchester, with over half a million books given away so far, and we hope passengers of all ages on the trams today enjoy our latest book giveaway and pick up a book and have a good read on us!". . Passengers travelling across Manchester's tram network were in for a surprise today (Friday 9 October) as 6,000 free books were given away on the city's trams by Read Manchester to mark World Mental Health which falls on Saturday.. The free book giveaway in partnership with Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) saw thousands of free reads placed on tram seats at the crack of dawn this morning - a book on every seat - and sent on their way from tram depots right across the tram network, ready to be picked up by passengers of all ages.. . The good read giveaway is part of Read Manchester's Take 10 to Read campaign which was first launched by Read Manchester in 2018 and is now promoted by the National Literacy Trust across the UK - and also this year worldwide through a world record attempt.. . The campaign highlights the wellbeing benefits of reading, and each year encourages people of all ages to spend 10 minutes reading on and around World Mental Health Day (10 October). to help improve their mental health.. . It complements wider work around the city by Read Manchester to encourage reading for enjoyment and help people discover the positive impact reading can have on learning, wellbeing and everyday life.. . This year's Take Ten to Read campaign, taking place during the National Year of Reading 2026, calls on people to explore their hobbies and interests through reading, with a simple message: whatever you're into, take 10 and read into it.. . candidates.lead: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men
candidates.evidence_text: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men Although some women were granted the right to vote in 1918, it was not until 1928 that all women over the age of 21 were granted the vote regardless of their occupation, wealth or ownership of property To mark this hugely significant milestone a Council motion has been set out to recognise and celebrate this moment in history It is no secret that Manchester played a huge part in the Women’s Suffrage movement. The Pankhurst name is known across the globe and is a byword for resilience and a refusal to give in to apparent insurmountable odds In 2018 a statue of Emmeline Pankhurst was proudly installed in St Peter’s Square and has since become a rallying point for people across the city to have their voices heard, and acts as a powerful reminder that history was made by women who refused to give up But the Pankhursts were also joined by thousands of ordinary Mancunian women whose names have been lost to history, but whose legacy still lives on a century later

candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

candidates.evidence_text: Libraries across the borough are teaming up with a local charity to help families access thousands of free pre-loved school uniforms and shoes As families continue to manage the high costs of school uniform, households cannot always afford the necessary items needed for their child This has led to growing demand for affordable alternatives, including a reliance on local charities like Uniform For All, which Rochdale Borough Council is working with to support those who need extra help Every day high-quality pre-loved items, including polo shirts, skirts, trousers, branded school blazers, coats and pumps, are given to families through the charity However, not every family has the resources to travel long distances to collect their orders That is why Rochdale’s library service is helping to collect these items so families can pick them up closer to where they live at their nearest library and save on additional travel costs

candidates.summary: The need for invasive post-mortems across Rochdale, Bury, and Oldham could be reduced by up to 80 per cent thanks to pioneering new digital autopsies
candidates.reason: LLM-review: Новая деталь: снижение инвазивных вскрытий до 80%, партнёры Anubix и TIC Health | Validator: corrected section routing before translation (section_routing:it_content). | Validator: news item is 21 days old (hard cutoff 14d), dropped regardless of update wording.

candidates.lead: The need for invasive post-mortems across Rochdale, Bury, and Oldham could be reduced by up to 80 per cent thanks to pioneering new digital autopsies
candidates.evidence_text: The need for invasive post-mortems across Rochdale, Bury, and Oldham could be reduced by up to 80 per cent thanks to pioneering new digital autopsies The innovative service is being delivered by the Coroner’s Office for Greater Manchester, in partnership with the NHS, specialist post-mortem imaging provider Anubix, and medical imaging provider TIC Health Working with pathologists, radiologists and mortuary staff at the Northern Care Alliance the coroner’s office will, where appropriate, provide computed tomography (CT) scanning to help inform a person’s cause of death Teams will use post-mortem imaging to check if a cause of death can be determined without the need for traditional invasive post-mortems, a process that can cause further distress to relatives during the grieving process A number of scans a week will be carried out using the new technology, with a long-term ambition of speeding up the service provided for relatives following the loss of a loved one Councillor Neil Emmott, leader of Rochdale Borough Council, said

candidates.evidence_text: A former pub transformed into sheltered accommodation for those struggling with homelessness has been described as a 'blueprint' to be replicated across the country Earlier this year, the former Queens Arms in Newtown was unveiled as a refurbished 14-bed sheltered accommodation, complete with kitchen and washing facilities, to give people in crisis a safe place to stay and receive further support to get back on their feet With homelessness in the national spotlight following Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s pledge to end rough sleeping, it is venues like the Queens Arms and the work of organisations like The Brick and Wigan Council that are being assessed to achieve these aims Councillor Susan Gambles, portfolio holder for housing and welfare, and chair of the homelessness and rough sleeping strategic partnership board, said: “There are some fantastic local partners that work collectively to support people at risk of homelessness, and we are so pleased “What comes across very strongly at their Queens Arms hub is that people are thriving there; they are positive, moving forward, and believing in themselves, and I think that is down to the facilities, the camaraderie, and the staff who care very deeply “This is the template that we should be using across the country, so we will continue championing these services and requesting more funding to be able to do even more like this.”

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: An immersive celebration of the greatest songs from the movies and the joy of singing together Gareth Malone – the man who got the nation singing – is back on the road this autumn with Sing-A-Long-A-Gareth: At The Movies , a brand-new live show celebrating the unforgettable songs that have helped make movie moments magical Following the success of last year’s singalong tour, which saw thousands of people across the country fill theatres with song, laughter and joy, Gareth now turns his attention to the big screen. From sweeping cinema classics to feel-good favourites, At The Movies will bring audie Gareth Malone is a fellow of the Royal Academy of Music where he studied with Janice Chapman and Jonathan Papp. He was awarded an honorary doctorate from the University of East Anglia and Freedom of the City of London in 2010. In 2012 he was made OBE in the Queen’s birthday honou He first appeared on TV in the three-part BAFTA award-winning series The Choir for BBC, tackling the task of teaching choral singing to people who have never had the chance, or experience to sing before. Followed by three further series; The Choir: Boys Don’t Sing, The Choir: Uns The end time for this event is tbc. More details will be published nearer to the event

candidates.evidence_text: ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян, один из самых ярких представителей современной русскоязычной стендап-сцены, приглашает вас на свой новый сольный концерт. Гарик известен как резидент Stand-Up Club #1, ведущий культового YouTube-шоу «Порараз Бирацца», участник проектов «Разгоны», «Книжный клуб», «Самый умный комик», «Стендап-комики», «Стендап Андеграунд». Кроме того, он является автором сольных концертов «Жизнь лучший драматург», «Жизнь худший драматург» и «И там, и сям» В новом концерте Гарик с присущими ему наблюдательностью, самоиронией и острым взглядом на происходящее расскажет о жизни, отношениях, эмиграции, повседневных абсурдах и обо всем, что превращает обычные ситуации в блестящую комедию. Не пропустите возможность провести вечер в компании одного из самых самобытных комиков своего поколения. Живой стендап, новые шутки и атмосфера, которую невозможно передать через экран. Хочешь, я приукрашу описание и добавлю несколько фактов? Например, Гарик был пятым участником группы the Beatles, но из-за природной скромности принял решение остаться в тени более пафосных коллег. Так же Гарик писал песни для групп Scorpions и Army of Lovers, является основателем гольф клуба в Майами, пробовал манго. Address: Big Belly Comedy Club, Unit 6 & 7, 30 Stamford St, London SE1 9LQ Doors: 19:00 Start: 19:40 Early Bird: £30 General Admission: £35 Late Bird: £40 18+ P.S. The interior showcases the works The famous cocktail menu will return, featuring favourites like the Pink Picante, Pomme Verte – a popular twist on an appletini, Belfast Coffee, the famous spicy pickle martini Especiado and the Pornstar Chic, crafted with homemade passionfruit sorbet Red Light also introduces a brand-new savoury snack menu, including, Boquerones, Pickled Guindilla peppers, Gordal olives, Mini Croissant Butter Blondies from Pollen and homemade Salted Popcorn Ice Cream. To complement the elevated look and taste, Red Light has curated energetic, “Red Light has always been about bringing people together over exceptional drinks in an inviting, unpretentious environment. Our new location gives us the space to realise that vision fully, with the same soul and now a proper home for cocktails, food, and great music.”

candidates.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

candidates.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
candidates.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

evidence_packet.title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

candidates.evidence_text: GM Business Growth Hub | Funding Strategy & Investor Pitching — Workshop Series Please ensure Javascript is enabled for purposes of website accessibility Home Events Funding Strategy & Investor Pitching — Workshop Series Funding Strategy & Investor Pitching — Workshop Series Date: 14 October 2026 End Date: 14 October 2026 Location: Manchester City Centre Time: 10:00 - 11:30 Theme: Funding Register A practical, step-by-step journey from funding strategy to confident pitch delivery. Funding can often feel confusing or overwhelming — especially when you're unsure where to start, what funders expect, or which type of finance is right for your business. This workshop series is designed to guide you through the full journey, from understanding funding options to delivering a confident and compelling pitch. When you're exploring investment, planning to grow, or considering funding to support your business, have you ever found yourself thinking: the process feels too complicated or overwhelming pitching feels nerve-wracking or unfamiliar you’re not sure what funders expect you’re unsure whether equity or debt is right for you you don’t have enough knowledge funding is only for ‘’high-growth’’ companies If any of the above feels familiar, this workshop series is designed to support you. We help remove these concerns by breaking everything down into clear, manageable steps. Delivered by our Access to Finance advisors, alongside funders and industry partners, the series helps you understand your options, strengthen your confidence, and build the practical skills needed to move forward. Across the sessions, you’ll explore funding strategy, assess the right type of finance for your business, understand key financials, and develop your pitch delivery. Whether you're early-stage or preparing for future opportunities, the workshops support you at your own pace — with clear guidance and no pressure or judgement. Workshop line-up: 09 Sep 2026 - Later Pitches Wednesday, 9th September 2026, 16:30 - 19:30 This event offers a unique opportunity for you to practice delivering your pitch with confidence, precision, and clarity. You will have the chance to present your ideas in a supportive setting, designed to help you develop your presentation skills and enhance your communication style when pitching to potential investors. You’ll receive valuable, constructive feedback from a panel of investment experts, enabling you to refine your pitch and make it more impactful for real-world scenarios. The feedback provided will empower you to identify areas for improvement and strengthen your presentation to maximise its appeal to potential investors. This workshop is delivered in collaboration with Plexal . Plexal is the innovation and growth company helping to strengthen the UK’s technology capabilities through collaboration. With teams in London, Manchester and Cheltenham, we work closely with government, industry, startups and academia to drive economic growth and reinforce national security. Founded by Delancey in 2017, Plexal delivers four core services: creating workspaces for innovators, running innovation programmes and consultancy, building regional tech clusters and helping SMEs scale strategically. Barclays is attending this event in a supportive capacity as an innovation and ecosystem partner only. Barclays is not responsible for organising or facilitating this event and is not arranging, promoting, soliciting or endorsing any investment focused activity that may take place, during or following it. 16 Sep 2026 - Understanding Equity Finance & Investor Expectations (In Person) Wednesday, 16th Sep 2026, 09:30 - 12:00 (In Person) If equity funding feels unfamiliar or complex, this session provides a clear, grounded understanding of how it works and what investors expect. We’ll walk through the process in practical terms, covering readiness, expectations, and key considerations for founders. You’ll learn: how equity finance works and whether it aligns with your goals what investors expect at different stages how valuation, dilution and ownership are approached how to prepare effectively before investor conversations You’ll leave with a stronger grasp of equity finance and greater clarity on your strategic options. This workshop is delivered in collaboration with GM Digital Security Hub (DiSH) . DiSH offers growing digital security businesses and the wider Greater Manchester community with access to business support, mentoring, dedicated grow

candidates.evidence_text: The first images of a major transformation of Stockport Railway Station have been revealed, with plans for a nine-figure overhaul designed to turn one of Greater Manchester’s busiest transport hubs into a more accessible, better-connected gateway to the town Stockport Council and Transport for Greater Manchester have unveiled proposals expected to cost more than £100m, with the station currently used by around four million passengers a year. The plans include new station buildings at both the town centre and Edgeley entrances, alongs The new footbridge would make the existing tunnel used to reach the platforms largely redundant, while improved accessibility and public realm works are also planned around the station. Land off Shaw Heath is also being safeguarded for a future Metrolink station, tying the propos The project forms part of a broader regeneration of Stockport, following the opening of the new Stockport Interchange and ongoing works around the town centre. The station sits at the heart of this expansion, with fast services reaching Manchester Piccadilly in under 10 minutes a The plans have been described as a “once in a generation” opportunity to reshape one of the North’s best-connected rail hubs, with the public now being invited to have their say on the proposals The consultation will run from 8 Oct to 17 Nov and invites residents, businesses, rail passengers and community groups to view the early proposals and have their say

From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. candidates.evidence_text: Football Amad Diallo Amad brands Man United loss a 'disgrace' in six-word reaction after Lisandro Martinez fury Manchester United's loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League has been branded a 'disgrace' by Amad after Lisandro Martinez also let rip following the game Amad dubbed Manchester United 's loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League a "f***ing disgrace", adding "I have no words" as a poor run of form continued These comments make up the caption of a post on his Snapchat account, which is verified as a Snap Star, denoted by the star next to the name on their profile. Amad , 24, started the match in Madrid among the substitutes and was introduced midway through the second half to replace Less than 10 minutes later, United had Leny Yoro sent off. "We (had) a fantastic season last season, and now we expect more from the top, from above, you know, to bring more players to compete, because many, many teams bring many players in as well, and today also, Atletico have an amazing team, and they deserved to win today."

candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Man United news: Michael Carrick sent sack verdict as boss warned of imminent squad 'explosion' Manchester United have made a poor start to the season under Michael Carrick and the manager has found himself under mounting pressure Add to prefer Manchester United boss Michael Carrick continues to be doubted following his team's lacklustre start to the season. But the club's new-look midfield has also been called into question Carrick's United have left a lot to be desired so far this term. They were ousted from the Carabao Cup by Brighton and have won just a single league game from six. Their latest home outing against Tottenham ended in a 1-1 draw, despite Spurs being reduced to 10 men in the 78th mi Their next league encounter will be a trip to Elland Road to face rivals Leeds United. The last time United made this journey, they drew 1-1 in January and Ruben Amorim was dismissed the following morning It's not just United's manager catching flak , however. Skipper Bruno Fernandes has been singled out by club icon Wayne Rooney for his performances along with his team-mates in midfield. The Manchester Evening News brings you the latest from Old Trafford Wayne Rooney has warned United that talismanic captain Bruno Fernandes is running out of patience. Rooney was asked about Fernandes on Stick to United and said: "He's fed up. I genuinely do think he looks, 'Oh, here we go again.' There are only so many times

candidates.evidence_text: A Southeast European studies seminar with Ivan Simic. His book ‘Sickle and Veil’ offers a comprehensive transnational history of communist gender policies towards Muslim minorities in Eastern Europe. candidates.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
